method: Editor-reviewed primary-source observations, not automated matching and not verified forecasts unless the original contains an explicit prediction.

observations.expected: The 2018 Renewable Energy Directive originally set a binding EU renewable-energy share target of at least 32% by 2030. This was a policy target, not a prediction that 32% would be achieved.
observations.happened: The 2030 binding target was raised to at least 42.5% in 2023. Eurostat reported a 25.2% renewables share of EU gross final energy consumption for 2024, leaving a 17.3-percentage-point gap to the revised 2030 target.
observations.verdict: Progress observed; 2030 target not yet due; no claim of final realization.

sources.finding: Directive revision raises target to at least 42.5%

observations.topic: EU net greenhouse gas reduction toward 2030
observations.expected: The EU policy objective is to reduce net greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030 relative to 1990, and become climate neutral by 2050. These are targets, not predictions.
observations.happened: The European Commission reported that provisional EU net greenhouse gas emissions in 2024 were 37.2% below 1990, within the scope of the EU climate target. The 2030 objective is not yet due.
observations.verdict: Observed emissions reductions; 2030 and 2050 objectives not yet verifiable as completed.

sources.finding: European Commission 2025 progress report gives 2024 net emissions reduction of 37.2% versus 1990
EEA says 2024 estimated net GHG emissions 37% below 1990; 55% 2030 goal not yet due
